# Princess Alexandra of Hanover Engaged! And the Ring Is from 1stDibs


Much like her grandmother Grace Kelly's ring, this jewel is a stunner.


by[Colleen Egan](https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/contributors/colleen-egan/)

Left: Ben-Sylvester Strautmann and Princess Alexandra of Hanover, seen here at the F1 Grand Prix of Monaco Gala in June in Monte-Carlo, Monaco, are engaged. Photo by Pascal Le Segretain/WireImage. Right: The engagement ring, which features a 4.8-carat yellow diamond, was purchased on 1stDibs from Antinori Fine Jewels.


When someone in the public eye gets engaged, especially a royal, the first question on a jewelry lover’s mind is: “What does the ring look like?” In the case of Princess Alexandra of Hanover, who recently became engaged to her partner of a decade, Ben-Sylvester Strauttman, we at 1stDibs were lucky enough to have all the details on the jewel. That’s because Strauttman purchased the ring on 1stDibs from[Antinori Fine Jewels](https://www.1stdibs.com/dealers/alessandra-antinori/) . We met with[Andrea Landolfi and Alessandra Antinori](https://www.1stdibs.com/introspective-magazine/antinori-fine-jewels/) , the Rome-based married couple behind the brand, to discuss the royal proposal and engagement ring trends.


Antinori says that Strauttman connected with them on 1stDibs, and the ring he ended up purchasing for Princess Alexandra features a 4.8-carat VVS1-clarity fancy yellow cushion-cut diamond flanked by a pair of trillion-cut white diamonds. The center stone is set in 18-karat yellow gold, and the trillion-cut stones are set in 18-karat white gold. “It’s a classic engagement ring,” Antinori says.


Antinori shared the sketches for the ring, which includes an 18-karat yellow gold setting for the center yellow diamond.


[Yellow diamonds have been growing in popularity](https://www.1stdibs.com/introspective-magazine/yellow-diamonds/) for years, both in engagement rings and other jewels — Zendaya, Lady Gaga and Anne Hathaway are among the celebrities who have sported yellow diamonds on the red carpet. “We’re seeing a lot of interest in fancy yellow diamonds, especially among younger people,” Antinori says.


She attributes this interest to factors like the rise of lab-grown diamonds and a corresponding desire to instead opt for fancy-colored diamonds or other gems. “In the last year, we have seen a lot of interest in colored gemstones, especially emeralds, rubies and sapphires,” Antinori says, adding that she’s also seen more interest in old mine-cut diamonds and unconventional stones like bubblegum-pink sapphires.


After Strauttman purchased the ring on 1stDibs, Landolfi and Antinori made plans to travel from Rome to Monte Carlo to hand deliver the ring ahead of the proposal. “We feel very grateful that he picked us,” Antinori says of Strauttman.


Grace Kelly


“She represents the future of the monarchy,” Antinori says of Princess Alexandra. The 27-year-old bride-to-be’s mother is Princess Caroline and grandmother is Grace Kelly, the Oscar-winning-actress-turned-royal whose style, elegance and beauty is legendary — after all, the Hermès Kelly bag is named after her. Kelly’s engagement ring from Prince Rainier III has also attained legendary status for its enduring design influence. The Cartier jewel, which Kelly famously wore in the 1956 film *High Society* , features a 10.48-carat emerald-cut white diamond flanked by a pair of baguettes. This was actually Kelly’s second engagement ring — the first was an eternity band set with diamonds and rubies, the colors of Monaco’s flag. Both rings are still in possession of the Monaco royal family, and the emerald-cut ring was[loaned to the V&A](https://www.instyle.com/grace-kelly-engagement-ring-11917303) for their 2025 Cartier exhibition.
